If you love bold flavors, hearty meals, and a little bit of Southern charm, a prawn creole recipe is your ticket straight to New Orleans food magic. This shrimp creole recipe combines creole prawns, tomato-based prawn stew, and aromatic spices to create a rich, comforting dish that’s perfect for weeknight dinners, family meals, or even a restaurant-style shrimp creole at home. From fresh shrimp to frozen shrimp, or jumbo prawns, this recipe works for all types of prawns.

What is Prawn Creole?

Prawn creole, also called shrimp creole, is a classic Louisiana cuisine dish that showcases Creole cuisine’s French-Spanish-African influences. Unlike Cajun shrimp, which often focuses on smokier flavors, Creole shrimp is all about a tomato-based sauce, aromatic spices, and fresh vegetables. You’ll find onion, bell pepper, green bell pepper, celery, and garlic simmering in tomatoes, crushed tomatoes, diced tomatoes, or tomato sauce, thickened slightly with tomato paste. Bay leaves, thyme, oregano, and parsley layer in that unmistakable authentic creole recipe taste.

 Ingredients for Homemade Prawn Creole Recipe

  • Prawns or shrimp (fresh, frozen, raw, peeled, or deveined)

  • Onion, bell pepper, celery, garlic

  • Tomatoes, crushed tomatoes, diced tomatoes, tomato sauce, tomato paste

  • Bay leaves, thyme, oregano, parsley

  • Paprika, cayenne pepper, black pepper, white pepper, salt

  • Creole seasoning, Cajun seasoning, hot sauce, Worcestershire sauce

  • Olive oil, butter, vegetable oil

  • Chicken stock or seafood stock

  • Optional: sugar, lemon juice, scallions, green onions

 How to Make Prawn Creole

 Step 1 – Prepping the Prawns

Whether using jumbo prawns, peeled prawns, or deveined prawns, start by rinsing them and patting dry. Season lightly with creole seasoning and a pinch of salt.

 Step 2 – Sautéing Vegetables

In a skillet or saucepan, heat olive oil or butter. Add onion, bell pepper, celery, and garlic, sautéing until soft and fragrant. This is the base of your aromatic seafood sauce.

 Step 3 – Building the Creole Sauce

Deglaze your pan with a splash of chicken stock or seafood stock. Add tomatoes, crushed tomatoes, tomato sauce, or tomato paste, along with bay leaves, thyme, oregano, parsley, paprika, and cayenne pepper. Simmer low and slow for a rich, thick sauce.

 Step 4 – Cooking the Prawns

Add your prawns or shrimp to the simmering sauce. Cook until they turn pink and are just opaque about 3–5 minutes depending on size. For extra tang, stir in lemon juice or hot sauce.

 Step 5 – Serving Suggestions

Serve over white rice, jasmine rice, basmati rice, brown rice, or cauliflower rice for a low-carb shrimp creole. Pair with crusty bread, French bread, garlic bread, or cornbread.

 Tips for the Best Prawn Creole

  • Use fresh shrimp for maximum flavor, but frozen shrimp works well too.

  • Adjust spice: spicy prawn creole vs mild shrimp creole depending on taste.

  • For keto shrimp creole, skip rice and serve with cauliflower rice or a green salad.

  • Make ahead shrimp creole: The sauce tastes even better the next day.

  • Experiment with Cajun vs Creole shrimp to understand the subtle differences in spice and sauce.

 Variations of Prawn Creole

  • Classic creole shrimp – stick to traditional creole shrimp recipe with all veggies and herbs.

  • Modern creole shrimp – use quick shrimp recipe techniques or pre-cooked prawns.

  • Healthy prawn recipe – lean on low-calorie shrimp recipe options and dairy-free shrimp creole.

  • High-protein seafood meal – great for keto shrimp creole or paleo creole shrimp fans.

 Serving & Storage Tips

  • Serve immediately over steamed rice or with side dishes for shrimp creole.

  • Store leftovercreole prawns in an airtight container in the fridge for 2–3 days.

  • Freeze homemade prawn creole for up to 2 months; thaw overnight in the fridge before reheating.

 Pairing Ideas

Creole-style seafood pairs beautifully with other Louisiana seafood dishes, New Orleans food classics, or even lighter options like low-carb shrimp creole for a keto-friendly dinner. Check out these keto dinner recipes for meals that complement your prawn creole with rice.

 FAQs About Prawn Creole

Q: What is prawn creole?
A: A tomato seafood stew with Louisiana tomato shrimp, aromatic seafood sauce, and spices.

Q: Is shrimp creole spicy?
A: It can be. Adjust cayenne pepper, hot sauce, or creole seasoning to your taste.

Q: Can I use frozen prawns for creole?
A: Absolutely! Just thaw them and pat dry before cooking.

Q: Best rice for prawn creole?
A: White rice, jasmine rice, or cauliflower rice for a low-carb version.
